description: Structured incident knowledge for the ai-padrao harness. Each entry maps a real defect pattern to the prevention rule (skill or lint config). Query by trigger_pattern before starting work that might re-introduce a known issue.

entries.symptom: ERROR [PackageLoader] The @fastify/static package is missing
entries.root_cause_summary: SwaggerModule.setup implicitly calls useStaticAssets() which requires @fastify/static as an undeclared peer

entries.symptom: res.setHeader is not a function (HTTP 500 on every request)
entries.root_cause_summary: Express API used against Fastify reply wrapper

entries.symptom: Nest can't resolve dependencies of the X service (?). Argument at index [0] is unavailable
entries.root_cause_summary: import type erases the runtime value reference that emitDecoratorMetadata relies on for design:paramtypes

auto_check.config: NestJS DI files (controllers, services, guards, strategies, interceptors, decorators) should never use `import type` for class references used in DI

entries.evidence: eslint --fix auto-introduced this bug; 10 unit tests regressed

entries.symptom: pnpm db:seed exits 0 with no DB writes
entries.root_cause_summary: Prisma's db seed command silently no-ops without a registered seed script

entries.symptom: GET /api/health returns 401; login endpoints reject all users
entries.root_cause_summary: Global JwtAuthGuard blocks all endpoints unless they opt out with @Public()

auto_check.should_exist: e2e test that hits /api/health without a token and expects 200

entries.symptom: docker compose build fails: Could not find Prisma Schema
entries.root_cause_summary: prisma generate runs before the schema is copied into the image

auto_check.rule: prisma generate must be preceded by COPY that includes prisma/schema.prisma

entries.symptom: ENOENT: no such file or directory, stat '.../@scope/config/file.js'
entries.root_cause_summary: ESLint 9 --config is a filesystem path, not a Node module specifier

entries.symptom: Bind for 127.0.0.1:<port> failed: port is already allocated
entries.root_cause_summary: Default well-known ports collide with sibling projects on the same host

auto_check.rule: Host-side port bindings should not use well-known defaults (1025, 8025, 3000, 5432, etc.) unless intentional

entries.symptom: Lint no-console warning; or startup banner written to stderr breaking log shippers
entries.root_cause_summary: console.warn satisfies no-console but writes to stderr; proper fix is Nest Logger with flushLogs

trigger_pattern.warning: peer-depends on @fastify/static or @nestjs/common that does not match

entries.symptom: pnpm install warns about peer dependency mismatch
entries.root_cause_summary: @nestjs/swagger@8 does not officially support NestJS 11; awaiting @nestjs/swagger@9

trigger_pattern.warning_emitted: The CJS build of Vite's Node API is deprecated

entries.symptom: Vite deprecation warning on every vitest run
entries.root_cause_summary: Vite falls back to deprecated CJS Node API when package.json lacks type:module

entries.symptom: Zero-day: skipped tests hide defects because they don't run. INC-005 was the trigger — /api/health returned 401 in production because no e2e test exercised it without a token.
entries.root_cause_summary: Project policy adopted on 2026-08-04: any pattern that masks a test (skip, todo, passWithNoTests, conditional describe/it) is forbidden. Either the test is real and runs, or it doesn't exist.

auto_check.command: find apps packages -type d \( -name node_modules -o -name .next -o -name dist -o -name .turbo -o -name coverage -o -name standalone \) -prune -o -type f \( -name '*.ts' -o -name '*.tsx' -o -name '*.js' -o -name '*.jsx' -o -name '*.json' \) -print | xargs grep -nE '\b(it|test|describe|context)\.skip\(|\b(xit|xdescribe|xtest)\b|\b(it|test)\.todo\(|--passWithNoTests|skip[[:space:]]*:'

entries.evidence: Pre-commit self-check: removing --passWithNoTests + adding env.client.spec.ts in apps/web triggered zero test failures

trigger_pattern.context: capture scripts that depend on jq silently no-op when jq is not installed

entries.symptom: The existing Prettier PostToolUse hook in ~/.claude/settings.json depends on jq. jq is not installed on this machine. The hook has been silently a no-op for months — every code change in the repo has gone through without ever being formatted by the hook.
entries.root_cause_summary: Capture scripts that depend on untested tools fail silently. The user has no way to know the hook is broken except by reading the hook's bash and noticing the `jq` call.

auto_check.rationale: python3 is the only required interpreter; future hooks MUST NOT add new top-level deps without updating this check.

entries.alura_principle: linter messages with correction instructions — the auto-check prints 'Fix: jq missing/broken; use python3 (see .harness/redact.py)' so the next maintainer knows the remediation path.

entries.symptom: Either events/<date>.jsonl is committed by mistake (leaking session state into the repo), or the agent refuses to capture because the dir doesn't exist (false negative).
entries.root_cause_summary: The events stream is session state, not source-of-truth. It MUST be gitignored. The digest output (.harness/digest/) is the human-reviewable artifact and stays committed.

auto_check.rationale: Anything committed to events/ becomes permanent. Per-session data must be allowed to be discarded.

entries.alura_principle: the sensor (capture) must never become the source of truth. The digest (L3) is the source of truth; the events stream is the volatile input.

entries.symptom: The daily agent silently stopped running. The harness kept capturing events but never converted them into learnings. After 7+ days, the system had ~10k events but the learnings.json was stale.
entries.root_cause_summary: Schedule-based jobs fail silently when the scheduler dies, the worker crashes, or the cron payload starts erroring. Without a freshness check, the operator has no signal that learning has stopped.

auto_check.rationale: 90000s = 25h, slightly over 24h to allow for timezone jitter but tight enough to catch a missed day.

entries.alura_principle: the sensor (capture) must have a heartbeat (digest) and the heartbeat must have a watchdog (this check).

entries.symptom: A live token appears in source code, the file is pushed, and the secret is now permanently in the git history. Even if the next commit removes it, the original is recoverable from the previous SHA.
entries.root_cause_summary: Tokens that travel through editor copy-paste, AI assistant context, or env var dumps end up in source code by accident. Once committed, the rotation cost is high (rotate, redact history, notify reviewers).

auto_check.rationale: Token-shaped strings in first-party source are always a leak. Tests are excluded because they may legitimately contain mock tokens.

entries.alura_principle: the sensor must catch leaks before they become permanent. The redactor (.harness/redact.py) is the seatbelt; the secret-shape scan is the airbag.

entries.symptom: L2 inline detector fires INC-002 or INC-003 confirmation prompts during documentation work (Write events under docs/decisions/, .harness/INCIDENTS.md, or .harness/learnings.json whose bodies quote the trigger patterns).
entries.root_cause_summary: The file-axis check uses substring matching against the trigger_pattern.files values declared in this file. Write events whose tool_input.content contains those substrings count as file-axis hits even when the Write targets a documentation path, not the runtime source the INC was designed to protect.
entries.alura_principle: the L2 detector must never mistake prose about a rule for code violating the rule. The path filter at pattern_match.py is the seatbelt; the regression test at .harness/test_pattern_match.py is the regression net.

entries.symptom: L2 detector false-positives on Read events, TodoWrite events, .claude/worktrees/<name>/ paths, and python3 << 'PY' heredocs. Every session action triggered INC-004 confirmation, even pure inspection events that never mutated runtime source.
entries.root_cause_summary: INC-017 added docs-path and diagnostic-bash filters but left four additional false-positive sources: (a) Read events count as file-axis hits even though they don't mutate; (b) TodoWrite events carry prose that substring-matches trigger_pattern.files; (c) worktree sessions share the main repo's event stream but operate on isolated branches; (d) the diagnostic-bash regex didn't match python3 << 'PY' heredocs; (e) the command lookup read event['command'] instead of event.tool_input.command (the actual Claude Code shape).
entries.alura_principle: the L2 detector must distinguish intent (Read vs Edit/Write) and context (worktree vs main repo, heredoc vs command). The exclusion list at pattern_match.py is the seatbelt; the auto-check is the airbag.

entries.symptom: L2 detector false-positives on multi-line Bash commands whose diagnostic tool (`find`, `cat`, etc.) is not on line 1. The bash scripts that wrap a `cd /path` + comment + diagnostic command slipped past `_DIAGNOSTIC_BASH_RE` because the regex anchored at `^`.
entries.root_cause_summary: INC-018 introduced `_DIAGNOSTIC_BASH_RE` with `^\s*(?:grep|cat|...)\b`, which only matches at position 0. Multi-line bash like `cd /home/.../padrao\n# Look for integration test files\nfind apps packages -name '*.spec.ts'` has `find` at byte position 50+, not position 0, so the diagnostic-exclusion didn't fire and the `*.spec.ts` substring in the command payload triggered INC-012.

prevention.section: Bash events matching read-only diagnostic regex (INC-017 + INC-018)

entries.alura_principle: a regex that anchors at the start of a string fails on multi-line input. Diagnostic bash detection must look for the diagnostic command anywhere in the multiline string.

entries.symptom: L2 detector false-positives on alphabetic symbols that substring-match unrelated words. Most painfully, `xit` matched `exit`, `exiting`, `exits` — every bash script that printed `echo "exit=$?"` false-fired INC-012 (no skipped tests).
entries.root_cause_summary: INC-012's symbol-axis check used `s in combined_text` plain substring semantics. For 3-letter alphabetic symbols like `xit`, this is too permissive — the substring appears in dozens of common English words.
entries.alura_principle: substring matching is not symbol matching. A 3-letter symbol like `xit` needs word boundaries to avoid matching the middle of `exit`. The Alura principle of correcting the false-positive at the source, not at the consumer.

entries.symptom: L2 detector fires INC-016 (no hardcoded secrets) on every Edit to apps/ or packages/, because pattern_match.py silently ignored the `shapes` field of INC-016's trigger_pattern. The file-axis gate fired alone — the shape check was a no-op.
entries.root_cause_summary: INC-016 declared its triggers as `shapes: [...]` (regex patterns for token shapes). pattern_match.py only checked `symbols`. The result: file-axis `≥2 hits under apps/**/*.ts` was sufficient to fire INC-016, even though the actual content had no token-shaped strings.
entries.alura_principle: silently ignoring a config field is worse than rejecting it — the user gets no signal that the field exists. Either implement the field or remove it from the schema.

entries.symptom: L2 detector fires INC-018 on every Edit to pattern_match.py, even when all required features are present. INC-018 is supposed to be a regression-detector (fires only when a feature is missing) but the code never checked the `required_features` field.
entries.root_cause_summary: INC-018 declared its trigger as `required_features: [...]` — an anti-pattern list. pattern_match.py ignored this field entirely, so file-axis alone (≥2 hits on .harness/pattern_match.py) fired INC-018 on every code edit.
entries.alura_principle: regression-detectors must gate on the regression, not on the file. INC-018 is about whether the features are still present — checking the file alone is a false-positive waiting to happen.

entries.symptom: L2 detector false-positives when the file-axis gate is satisfied but the symbol-axis evidence lives in completely unrelated events. The clearest case: any Edit to `.harness/learnings.json` (which legitimately contains `import type`, `xit`, and `ghp_` as trigger-pattern literals) bumps the file-axis count for INC-003/INC-012/INC-016, and the symbol-axis then matches the literal trigger text in the Edit body — every configuration edit triggers the patterns it configures.
entries.root_cause_summary: pattern_match.py built `combined_text` from every event in the window (Read, Write, Edit, Bash — all 20 events). The symbol-axis check (`s in combined_text`) then matched trigger literals that happened to appear anywhere in the window, including legitimate configuration files. The semantic fix: when `trigger_pattern.files` is declared, restrict the symbol-axis text to the SAME events that count toward the file-axis gate. Trigger literals living in unrelated events stop mattering.

auto_check.expected: scoped symbol-axis text built from file-axis hits only

entries.alura_principle: the file-axis and symbol-axis must address the same events. Otherwise documents and configuration files that legitimately quote trigger patterns become indistinguishable from violations. The Alura principle of correctness over cleverness — the simpler combined-text approach is wrong even when it works most of the time.

trigger_pattern.context: PASSIVE — INC-024 is now RESOLVED via .openspec/changes/inc-024-detector-type-vs-di/. The original trigger used to fire when a legitimate `import type` for a type/interface slipped through INC-003's tightened file-axis gate. With INC-003's new `symbol_filters.safe_suffixes` classifier, that emission is suppressed at the matcher layer.

entries.symptom: L2 detector fires INC-003 on every legitimate `import type` for an interface or type alias in a NestJS-adjacent file. The clearest case: `import type { AuditContext }` in `audit-context.spec.ts` (an interface returned by AsyncLocalStorage, not a DI'd class) — same `import type` syntax, completely different semantic risk. The current detector counts both as DI violations.
entries.root_cause_summary: INC-003's trigger pattern is a substring match on `import type` over any file under `apps/api/src/**/*.ts`. The pattern cannot distinguish between (a) `import type { PrismaService }` in a controller constructor (DI risk — `design:paramtypes` is undefined) and (b) `import type { AuditContext }` in a spec file (pure type — erased by TS at compile time, no runtime impact). Both match the same literal substring. INC-023's scoped symbol-axis correctly limits the matcher to file-axis hits but does not filter by file semantics (test vs production) or binding semantics (class vs type).

prevention.section: Type-only `import type` excluded from INC-003 (INC-024) — pending design decision

auto_check.command: Verify INC-003 entries' trigger_pattern.symbol_filters.safe_suffixes contains the eight registered suffixes and that pattern_match.py's TYPE_ONLY_SUFFIXES tuple stays in sync.

entries.alura_principle: the right place to fix a detector that fires on legitimate code is the detector itself, not the operator. Until the four candidate fixes are evaluated, operators must confirm each prompt manually — which is acceptable cost for a low-frequency, low-impact prompt, but the long-term answer is making the detector understand binding semantics.

trigger_pattern.context: ACTIVE — INC-028 fires when a touched file lacks the Diátaxis-classified documentation artifact for its kind: JSDoc with @example or @remarks on every exported symbol, README.md on every bounded context / feature folder, ADR for non-obvious decisions, runbook for infra changes. NOTE: INC-027 is the cyclomatic-complexity check (existing) — this entry deliberately uses INC-028 to avoid id collision.

entries.symptom: Documentation drift reappears within a sprint because the harness had no build-time signal for missing or stale docs. The 2026-08-04 one-shot audit fixed the visible drift but every subsequent PR that landed code without its doc re-introduced the gap.
entries.root_cause_summary: The harness has INC-001..INC-026 auto-checks for code and config, but zero auto-checks for the documentation surface. The 'documentation fixes don't require SDD' rule in AGENTS.md is a guideline, not enforcement.

auto_check.command: Run three sub-checks: (1) every apps/api/src/contexts/<bc>/ and apps/web/src/features/<feature>/ has README.md; (2) for each .ts/.tsx in git diff --name-only --cached, public-surface JSDoc coverage ≥ 80% via bin/jsdoc-coverage.py; (3) every ADR-NNN reference in the repo resolves to docs/decisions/ADR-NNN-*.md via bin/adr-ref-check.py.

entries.alura_principle: any project rule that lives only in AGENTS.md (a guide) is weaker than the same rule living as an auto-check in .harness/check.sh (an enforcement). When adding a new category of project hygiene — docs, lint, formatting, naming — ask 'can this be a check() call in check.sh?' If yes, prefer the auto-check; the prose becomes a cross-link.

trigger_pattern.context: PASSIVE — INC-029 fires only when the L2 detector blocks a legitimate read-only operation (lint, typecheck, format-check, test list). The incident template below documents the *symptom class*, not a specific command. The actual mitigation lives in `_DIAGNOSTIC_BASH_RE` in `pattern_match.py` (extension of INC-019) and the `HARNESS_L2_ENABLED` env var added to `detect.sh`.

entries.symptom: L2 detector (INC-012, 'no skipped tests') fires confirmation prompts when the operator runs `pnpm exec eslint`, `pnpm exec prettier --check`, `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`, `pnpm test --list`, or `pnpm exec playwright test --list` against a file that legitimately contains `test.skip(...)` as a placeholder (e.g. inside a placeholder test fixture or a file under active authoring). The detector's file-axis counts the lint bash event, the symbol-axis finds `.skip(` in the file content, and the gate fires — even though the operator is *reading* the file, not *writing* a new skip.
entries.root_cause_summary: INC-019's diagnostic-bash filter was scoped to read-only commands that *do not mention runtime paths* (grep/cat/head/ls/find/md5sum). It missed the much larger category of linter invocations that *do* mention runtime paths (`eslint path/to/file.ts`). Combined with the symbol-axis scoped_text from INC-023 — which now legitimately reads file content via `_event_text` — the result is over-eager blocking. The fix has two parts: (1) extend `_DIAGNOSTIC_BASH_RE` to match `eslint|tsc|prettier|vitest|jest|playwright` invocations as read-only, and (2) add `HARNESS_L2_ENABLED` to `detect.sh` so an operator can globally opt out without modifying `~/.claude/settings.json`.

auto_check.expected: Both grep matches present (the regex set in pattern_match.py AND the env-var gate in detect.sh).

entries.alura_principle: A detector that fires on every legitimate read of a file becomes noise, and noisy detectors get globally muted — at which point the catch on real reincarnations is also muted. The two-part fix (extend the filter + add an opt-out escape hatch) lets the detector stay strict on writes while becoming invisible on reads.

trigger_pattern.context: PASSIVE — INC-030 fires only when an L2 detector entry declares ONLY a file-axis (no symbols/shapes/required_features) AND the file-axis is the enforcer for a soft-reminder category. The mitigation lives in `pattern_match.py:_RUNTIME_SKIPPABLE_CATEGORIES`.

entries.symptom: Soft-reminder INC entries that rely solely on the file-axis pollute every operator interaction: any Edit/Write to a path inside the file globs triggers the gate, including workflow-irrelevant commands like `pnpm exec eslint path/to/file.ts` or `git diff` quoted in a commit. INC-028 (documentation coverage) is the canonical example — its `files: apps/api/src/**` globs catch EVERY code edit, and the entry has no symbol/shape/required_features axis to verify intent, so the gate fires on noise. Build-time enforcement (`check.sh` doc_coverage auto_check) already runs at PR time and catches real drift, making the L2 emit redundant.
entries.root_cause_summary: Two layers of enforcement existed: L2 runtime detector (fires on every interaction to remind operators) and `check.sh` auto_check (fires at PR pre-commit/build). For soft-reminder categories — `documentation-coverage`, `process-discipline` — the build-time auto_check is the right cadence and the L2 emit adds only noise. The fix: skip L2 emit when an entry's category is in a soft-reminder set AND the entry has no symbols/shapes/required_features axis. Hard-gate categories (security, DI, schema) keep firing — their risk is too high to delegate to build-time only.

auto_check.expected: match present (the soft-reminder category set is defined in pattern_match.py)

entries.alura_principle: A detector's job is to catch real reincarnations, not to remind on every interaction. If a project rule has both a soft prose form (AGENTS.md) and an auto_check at build time (check.sh), the runtime L2 detector should defer to the build hook for low-stakes categories. Hard-stakes categories (anything that can prod-bug a customer) keep firing at every relevant interaction regardless.

suggested_agent_rule_updates.content: Before any change involving [NestJS interceptors/guards/decorators] [Docker] [ESLint config] [Prisma seed] [Swagger] [JWT auth], invoke the matching skill. See .harness/INCIDENTS.md for full history.
Promoted 2026-08-04: skipped tests are forbidden. See AGENTS.md §No skipped tests for the full rule and .harness/check.sh INC-012 for the auto-check.

Promoted 2026-08-04: the harness learns from every event. Capture (L1), inline detection (L2), daily digest (L3), and enforcement (L4) form a closed loop. Skipping or bypassing the inline detector is a forbidden action — see AGENTS.md §Continuous learning.
